## Declarations and implementations

```plato

// A finite-impulse-response filter: the output is the convolution of the
// input with Taps, where Taps[0] weights the current sample.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finite_impulse_response)
type FirFilter
    implements IValue
{
    Taps: Array<Number>;
}

// An infinite-impulse-response filter in direct form. Feedforward
// coefficients (b) weight current and past inputs; feedback coefficients (a)
// weight past outputs, with FeedbackCoefficients[0] normalized to 1.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinite_impulse_response)
type IirFilter
    implements IValue
{
    FeedforwardCoefficients: Array<Number>;
    FeedbackCoefficients: Array<Number>;
}

//==
// # Rate conversion and mixing

// The interpolation used when resampling a signal to a new rate.
type SignalResampling = ZeroOrderHold | Linear | CubicHermite | WindowedSinc;

// A sample-rate conversion request: the source and target rates and the
// interpolation used between them.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sample-rate_conversion)
type SampleRateConversion
    implements IValue
{
    SourceRate: Frequency;
    TargetRate: Frequency;
    Interpolation: SignalResampling;
}

// The gain law of a crossfade between two signals: gains sum to 1 (Linear),
// squared gains sum to 1 (EqualPower), or smooth-stepped linear (SCurve).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fade_(audio_engineering))
type CrossfadeLaw = Linear | EqualPower | SCurve;

// A crossfade description: the gain law and the time taken to move fully
// from one signal to the other.
type CrossfadeParameters
    implements IValue
{
    Law: CrossfadeLaw;
    Duration: Duration;
}

//==
// # Signal envelopes and generators
//
// Pure descriptions of synthesized signals: amplitude envelopes, noise
// sources, and periodic waveform generators. Every type here is a parameter
// record, deterministic where it is seeded; the sampled results they describe
// are declared in the first section above.

// An attack-decay-sustain-release amplitude envelope. Sustain is the level
// held after decay as a proportion of peak; the other stages are durations.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envelope_(music))
type AdsrEnvelope
    implements IValue
{
    Attack: Duration;
    Decay: Duration;
    Sustain: Proportion;
    Release: Duration;
}

// The spectral color of a noise generator: White is flat, Pink -3 dB/octave,
// Brown -6 dB/octave, Blue +3 dB/octave.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colors_of_noise)
type NoiseColor = White | Pink | Brown | Blue;

// A pure description of a noise generator: spectral color, peak amplitude,
// and the seed of its deterministic random sequence.
type NoiseSignal
    implements IValue
{
    Color: NoiseColor;
    Amplitude: Number;
    Seed: Integer;
}

// The shape of a periodic test or synthesis waveform. Pulse carries its
// duty cycle: the high fraction of each period.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waveform)
type Waveform
    = Sine
    | Square
    | Triangle
    | Sawtooth
    | Pulse(DutyCycle: Proportion);

// A pure description of a periodic waveform generator. Phase offsets the
// start of the cycle.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_generator)
type WaveformGenerator
    implements IValue
{
    Waveform: Waveform;
    Frequency: Frequency;
    Amplitude: Number;
    Phase: Angle;
}
```
